name: The First Stroke
hint: Click or drag beside Suzu to paint a stroke. Stepping into a yokai cuts it. Press Space to sheathe and end the stroke. Never rest on red.
story: Heian-kyō, the hour of the Ox. In the temple at the capital's edge hangs the great scroll that bound the Night Parade of a Hundred Demons. Tonight it hangs blank.
Tamamo-no-Mae has licked the ink from the paper, Suzu. What was painted now walks.
Take the brush-blade. Every stroke you draw is at once a step and a cut. Paint them back where they belong.
千里の道も一歩から. A road of a thousand ri begins with one step. Yours begins with one stroke.
And if my hand shakes, Master?
Then you will be merely strong. Be 上手 — skilled. Strength spills ink. Skill spends none.
after: Two lanterns, two strokes. The paper remembers them already. Go on to the gate.
And when your hand does slip — it will — remember 弘法も筆の誤り. Even Kōbō Daishi's brush made mistakes. Take the stroke back and paint it again.

name: The Measure of Distance
hint: Momentum 勢: each step in a straight line adds 1 to the cut that follows it. A standing cut deals 1, a one-step run 2, two steps 3. Let the oni come to the right distance.
story: Beneath the broken beams of Rashōmon something red is breathing.
An oni's hide turns a lazy blade. Do not hack at it. Give your stroke room to run — that room is called ma-ai, 間合.
So I should not rush in.
after: It came to me, and I was already moving.
That is the whole of swordsmanship. The rest is footnotes.
急がば回れ, Suzu. If you are in a hurry, go the long way round.

name: The Pincer
hint: Two oni close from both sides. You cannot be at the right distance from both at once — so decide who arrives first.
story: One enemy is a question of distance. Two enemies are a question of order.
Only if you stand still and let them agree on it.
after: You made them take turns. Good. The captain of the gate will not be so obliging.

name: Ibaraki of the Gate
hint: The great oni has three lives. Only a full two-step run cuts it down in one blow.
story: Little painter. A warrior once took my arm at this gate. I took it back. What will you take from me?
Ha! Then come and measure me.
after: The oni thins to a wash of ink, then to a line, then to a place on the scroll that had been waiting for him.
鬼の目にも涙, they say: even an oni's eye can hold a tear. I think he was glad to stop.
North, now. The tengu of Kurama once taught a boy named Ushiwaka to fight. Ask them, politely, to teach you.

name: Wind in the Cedars
hint: A tengu never moves, but its fan sweeps its whole row and column. Stone breaks the wind — and so does any yokai standing in the way.
story: Mount Kurama. The cedars are older than the capital, and the wind in them has opinions.
Another child with a stick. Ushiwaka at least brought rice cakes.
I brought a blank scroll, great tengu, and you are missing from it.
Hm! Then climb. My nephews will fan you off the mountain if you walk in the open.
after: You used my own cedars against me. Acceptable. I will show you how Ushiwaka crossed the Gojō bridge rail.
Suzu learns 縮地 SHUKUCHI — the shrinking of the earth. Once per stage, leap over one tile of anything.

name: The Shrinking Earth
hint: Press 1, then a direction, to leap two tiles over water, stone or yokai. A leap counts as a step of run-up.
story: Shukuchi is not jumping. You fold the ground like paper and step across the crease.
Once is a technique. Twice is a habit. Spend it where nothing else will do.
after: Hmph. The boy took a month.

name: Crossed Fans
hint: Two fans sweep the top row and both edges. Cross the stream where the wind cannot follow.
story: One fan you can hide from. My nephews have learned to stand where their winds cross.
Then somewhere between them is a place neither can see.
Hm. Find it before they find you.
after: You walked through a crossfire as if it were a garden. One more lesson, then.

name: Sōjōbō's Court
hint: Read the red wash before every stroke. Where can you end safely — and what can stand between you and the wind?
story: Last lesson. Two fans, one bridge, and a guest from the capital who dislikes you.
I invited a problem. Solve it.
after: Go south to Shinoda. The white fox there owes the court of painters a favour. And child — foxes do not fight. They agree with you until you lose.
One more thing. When a person grows conceited, your people say 天狗になる: he has 'become a tengu'. I resent the phrase. See that you do not earn it.

name: Fox Fire
hint: The fox copies every step you take. Chase it and it flees at your pace — unless something stops it and not you.
story: Shinoda Forest. Pale fires hang between the camphor trees, and one of them has ears.
Of course. It is being polite. A fox walks in the footsteps of whoever is watching.
You cannot outrun a mirror, little brush. Find the place where it has no step left.
after: Good. You stopped chasing and started arranging.

name: Kuzunoha's Leaves
hint: Press 2, then a direction, to paste a ward 結界 beside you. No yokai may enter it; you may. A ward is a wall you choose.
story: My son Seimei wrote wards that could stop a star. Take one of his leaves.
Suzu learns 結界 KEKKAI — once per stage, paste a ward on a tile beside you. Yokai cannot enter it and the tengu's wind cannot cross it.
A fox to herd, and a great tengu at the end of a stone lane. There is no cover in that lane but what you bring.
after: You see it now. Every wall is a hand that holds your enemy still.
They have a saying for how you looked an hour ago: 狐につままれる. Pinched by a fox. You are learning to pinch back.

name: Bewitched
hint: Two foxes mirror every step while an oni walks you down. Each step you take moves three pieces — count all of them.
story: A fox alone is a riddle. A fox while something chases you is a different animal.
Every step I take to flee, they take too.
Then never flee. Only ever go somewhere.
after: There. You moved once and three things went where you wanted.

name: The Shinoda Mirror
hint: A ward also breaks the tengu's wind. One leaf, three uses — choose.
story: Tamamo-no-Mae is my elder by eight tails. She will copy you perfectly, and smile while she does it.
Then I will give her something worth copying.
Mm. Practise on my cousins first.
after: She has gone east. But the road east runs under Mount Ōe, and the oni king Shuten-dōji has shut it. A man named Tsuna keeps watch there. He has history with oni.

name: The Ogres' Gate
hint: Three oni, and the great one in front. A ward stops an oni as surely as stone — and a stopped oni is standing at a distance you chose.
story: Mount Ōe. The road east runs under it, and the road has been shut with a gate of horn and iron.
I am Watanabe no Tsuna. I took an arm from Ibaraki at Rashōmon once. I hear you finished the job.
His master Shuten-dōji holds this mountain. His gate-wardens come three at a time. Do not let them arrive three at a time.
after: Hah! You fight like someone who has read the ending. Come, the path climbs.

name: Valley Wind
hint: The great tengu watches the whole west bank and its row. The oni do not care about wind. Use one to hide from the other.
story: A tengu has taken service with the oni king. It guards the stream; the oni guard the tengu.
Then they stand in each other’s way.
...I had not thought of it like that.
after: You used an oni as a windbreak. I am going to tell that story for years.

name: The Feast
hint: Lanterns, a fox, two oni. Nothing here is new; everything here is at once.
story: The oni king’s hall. Lanterns sway though there is no wind, and something laughs along with every laugh.
In the old tale we poisoned his wine. He has stopped accepting gifts.
Then we will have to be good instead of clever.
after: The hall is quiet. He will have heard that.

name: Shuten-dōji
hint: The oni king has five lives and walks toward you like any oni. Even a full run cuts only three. You will need two perfect arrivals.
story: A girl with a paintbrush. Raikō brought an army and a lie.
Good. I am tired of being beaten by tricks. Come and do it properly.
after: The oni king laughs once, hugely, and is a red line on the scroll, cup still raised.
鬼に金棒, an iron club in an oni's hand: nothing stronger, we say. You never let him swing it.
The road east is open. The fox went to Nasu, where the grass dies in a ring. Find the monk Gennō. He hits things.

name: The Killing Stone
hint: Yūrei pass through stone and water as if they were mist. They cannot pass a ward.
story: Nasu Moor. Birds that cross it fall. In the middle stands a stone, and around the stone, those who came too near.
Don't breathe so deep, girl. The dead here are not angry. They are only cold, and you are warm.
Rocks are for the living. Stand where they must come to you one at a time.
after: Clean work. Now let me teach you the only sutra I ever finished.
Suzu learns 喝 KATSU — once per stage, a shout that hurls every yokai beside you one tile away. Into water, they are gone. Into a wall, they are hurt.

name: Gennō's Shout
hint: Press 3 to shout. Everything beside you is thrown one tile. Water swallows yokai whole — let the river do the cutting.
story: KATSU! — Like that. From the belly.
That would not frighten a sparrow. Again, when it matters.
after: There. Even the stone flinched. She is waiting for you beyond the dead grass.

name: Grudges
hint: Ghosts that ignore the river, oni that cannot swim. One shout, one ward, one leap — and each can only be spent once.
story: Past here she has gathered everything that ever hated anyone.
Does it matter? You only ever fight the ones standing next to you.
after: Mm. Nothing wasted. Go on, then. She is waiting, and she hates waiting.

name: Tamamo-no-Mae
hint: She has five lives and walks in your footsteps. A full run cuts three. Where has she no step left?
story: So this is the hand they sent. Ink on the fingers, mud on the hem.
I was the jewel of three courts, child. I will move as you move, think as you think, and I have had nine hundred years to practise.
Then you already know how this ends.
after: Nine tails fold into nine lines of ink. In the scroll's crowd a fox in court robes is, very slightly, smiling.
覆水盆に返らず. Spilled water does not return to the tray. Ink, it seems, can.
You spilled nothing, Suzu. And yet — unroll it further.
The end of it is still blank.
She was the one who freed them. She was never the last of them.

name: Thin Ice
hint: Ice 氷: step onto it and you slide until something stops you, for one drop of ink. Every tile you slide is a step of run-up.
story: The scroll is whole from the capital to Nasu. But its far end is still bare paper, and the bare paper is cold to the touch.
The north never came back, Suzu. Snow country. The ones who fled there were never afraid of you.
Then you cannot choose where you stop. Choose where you start.
after: You let the ice carry the blade. Good. It will carry you into worse, too.

name: The Umbrella
hint: Kasa-obake hop two tiles toward you, straight over anything. They are never where an oni would be.
story: Something is coming down the white road in great idiotic bounds.
A hundred years in a doorway and anything grows a temper. Mind its rhythm. It only knows one.
after: Everything is easy once it is counted.

name: Blizzard
hint: On ice you cannot choose where you stop — only where you start. The great tengu sees the whole length of its row and column.
story: A tengu has come north for the wind. It can see across the whole frozen field.
And I cannot stop on it.
Then be seen only where it does not matter.
after: Mm. You slid the length of its gaze and were gone before it blinked.

name: Yuki-onna
hint: Yuki-onna has three lives and drifts toward you through anything, like a ghost. On ice there is no standing still.
story: You are warm. I can hear it from here.
You are not on the scroll.
I was. I was a white space between two pine trees. I did not like it.
I will paint you the whole winter.
...Come onto the ice, then, and show me.
after: Snow falls onto the paper and stays. Between two pines there is now a woman, looking out.
石の上にも三年. Three years on a stone and even the stone grows warm. She has waited longer than that.
South again. The river spirits have noticed the scroll filling and gone to ground. Or rather, to water.

name: The Kappa
hint: Kappa never leave the water. They swim toward you and drag at anything on the bank beside them. Cut them from dry land.
story: A green pool at the bend of a river. The water is still in a way that water should not be.
after: They cannot follow me onto land.
And you cannot follow them off it. Remember which of you that troubles more.

name: Sumo
hint: A shout throws land yokai into the water — and throws kappa against whatever is behind them. Water is a weapon for both sides here.
story: We have friends now. Big friends. Dry friends.
after: Hah. The river took what the blade did not need to.

name: The Rapids
hint: Water is a wall to you and a road to them. You have one leap. Decide which bank it is for.
story: A tengu on the high ground, a kappa in the crossing, and company on this side.
after: I spent it going, not coming back.
There was nothing to come back for. Well judged.

name: Lord of the Pool
hint: The kappa lord has four lives. Wherever there is water, the bank beside it belongs to him.
story: I am the lord of this pool and of four hundred pools. I have never lost a bout.
Because you never leave the water.
That is called knowing your ground. You should try it.
after: 河童の川流れ. Even a kappa is carried off by the river, they say. I had hoped never to be the example.
The pool goes clear. On the scroll, a river fills in from source to sea, and four hundred small green heads bob in it.
The burial ground at Adashino is next, Suzu. Nothing there was ever properly put to rest.

name: Ghost-Fire Road
hint: Fire 火 burns you if you end a stroke on it; passing over is free. Nurikabe are walls that must be broken: three lives, no malice, always in the way.
story: Adashino, where the capital once left its dead. The paper here is scorched, and the road across it is lit with fires nobody set.
There are walls where there were no walls.
Nurikabe. They do not strike. They simply stand between you and a clean ending. Count them as enemies anyway.
after: You did not rest on the fire once. Go on.

name: The Barrier
hint: A wall will hide you from a tengu as well as stone does — until you break it.
story: 壁に耳あり、障子に目あり. The walls have ears and the paper doors have eyes. Here, it is literally so.
They have built themselves a checkpoint. Wind behind walls.
If I break the wall I lose my cover.
Then the order you do things in is the whole problem. As usual.

name: The Hundred
hint: Everything you have met, on one board. Nothing here is new. Read it twice before your first stroke.
story: And here they all are, the stragglers, drawn up across the road like a festival that has forgotten what it is for.
Master, how many is a hundred?
More than you can fight. Exactly as many as you can solve.
after: 勝って兜の緒を締めよ. After the victory, tighten your helmet cord.
One left. It has been walking behind the parade this whole time, picking up what fell.

name: Gashadokuro
hint: The great skeleton has seven lives and strikes all eight tiles around it, corners too. A full run cuts three. Arrive, and be gone.
story: It is made of everyone the parade left unburied. It has nothing to say. It is only hungry, and very large.
Then I will be small, and exact.
after: The bones come apart gently, like a held breath let go, and lie down in the last blank hand-width as a field of white grass.
夏草や 兵どもが 夢の跡. Summer grasses: all that is left of the warriors' dreams.
The scroll is whole. A hundred demons, a road, a river, a winter. In one corner, very small, a girl with a brush.
I had the upper hand, Master.
上手. Yes. That is how it is written.

name: Mount Osore
hint: Nothing here is new. Everything here is together.
story: Mount Osore, in the far north, where the living go to speak with the dead. Sulphur, pinwheels, grey water.
I have nothing left to teach you about any one of them, Suzu.
And about all of them at once?
That was never something that could be taught.
after: Mm. Go on. I will only be in the way.

name: The Procession
hint: The last hand-width of the scroll. Read every board twice.
story: The last hand-width of the scroll. A drum is beating somewhere ahead, slowly, and everything that has not yet been painted is walking toward it.
It is a parade. It was always a parade. Go and be the end of it.

name: The Kōan
hint: Kōan 公案: one stroke, and only one. Nothing moves but you, and whatever copies you. Sheathe the brush with anything left standing and you begin again.
story: The scroll is whole and hangs again in its temple. Tessai looks at it for a long time, then takes down a single sheet of blank paper.
You can end a hundred demons in five strokes each. Now end them in one.
Master Hakuin asked: you know the sound of two hands clapping. What is the sound of one? 隻手の声. I am asking you the same thing with a brush.
One stroke for all of them?
One stroke is all anyone ever really has. The rest is correction.

name: Wet Ink
hint: Wet ink 墨: the stroke you just painted stays wet for one turn. No yokai can cross it and no wind passes it. Paint your own walls.
story: You have always thought of the stroke as where you went. Think of it as what you left.
For a breath. Long enough to matter.
after: You hid behind your own handwriting. Good.
余白の美. The beauty of what is left blank. You are beginning to choose it on purpose.

name: Ensō
hint: Ensō 円相: with the long brush (7 ink), end a stroke beside the tile where it began and the circle closes. Any yokai inside it is bound at once, however strong.
story: A circle, drawn in one breath. The monks say it shows the mind of whoever drew it. Tessai's is slightly flat on one side.
吾唯足知, it says on the basin at Ryōan-ji. I know only what is enough. A circle is exactly enough.
Take the long brush. Do not cut this one. Go around it.
And when I come back to where I began?
Then there is nothing left inside to fight.
after: There was nowhere for it to go that was not you.

name: The Stone Garden
hint: Garden 石庭: there are no yokai here. Rake every open tile in one stroke, never crossing your own line. The stones stay where they are.
story: Behind the temple is a garden of raked gravel and fifteen stones. It is said that from wherever you sit, one of the fifteen is always hidden.
It is a garden, and it needs raking. 一に掃除、二に信心. First sweep; then believe.
after: Not a stone moved, not a line crossed. The monks will think a monk did it.

name: The Gate
hint: Gate 鳥居: you need not fight. Reach the torii and the stage is won, however many yokai are left behind you.
story: Today you will not cut anything at all.
By arriving. 三十六計逃げるに如かず: of the thirty-six stratagems, the best is to run.
after: And you are here. Which of you won?

name: The Ink Stone
hint: Ink stone 硯: ink you do not spend is kept for the next stroke, up to 8. Stand still to grind; then paint the long line, even a circle (7 ink).
story: Tessai takes back the long brush and hands her the old short one, and a worn black stone with a hollow in it.
墨を磨るは病夫の如く. Grind the ink like an invalid: slowly, with no strength at all.
Then wield the brush like a warrior. But the grinding comes first.
after: You waited. Most never learn that the waiting is part of the stroke.

name: No Sword
hint: No sword 無刀: your brush will not cut here. Bind with the circle, drown or break with the shout, or simply go around.
story: Yagyū Muneyoshi once stood before Tokugawa Ieyasu with empty hands and took the wooden sword out of his grip. 無刀取り. Ieyasu made the Yagyū his teachers that day.
You are taking my blade away.
I am telling you that you never needed it.
after: 無手勝流. The school of winning with no hands. Old Bokuden would have approved.

name: Daruma
hint: Daruma 達磨: a blow only topples it, once in a stroke, and it rises again when the turn ends. Strike it in two separate strokes. While it is down it cannot strike you.
story: On the temple shelf sits a row of round red figures with no arms, no legs and a great deal of patience.
Bodhidharma sat facing a wall for nine years, until his legs fell away. 面壁九年. These are his portrait.
They fall over when I touch them.
And get up. 七転び八起き. Fall seven times, rise eight. You will have to knock each one down twice, and mean it both times.
after: Good. Now you know what it is to fight something more stubborn than you are.

name: Tanuki
hint: Tanuki 狸: it sits as a stone with a leaf on it, and stone cannot be cut. End a stroke on a tile beside it, or startle it with a shout, and it shows itself. After that it is a yokai like any other.
story: One of the garden stones has a leaf on its head. It did not have a leaf yesterday. It was not, strictly speaking, there yesterday.
狸寝入り. Tanuki sleep: pretending, with great commitment. You cannot cut a stone. Go and stand beside it until it is embarrassed.
after: 化けの皮が剥がれる. The disguise peels off. It always does, if you are willing to wait next to it.

name: The Red Thread
hint: Hitodama 人魂: soul-flames joined by a red thread. They do no harm, but one that is put out relights at the end of the turn while any other still burns. Put them all out in a single stroke, or be standing where the fallen one would rise.
story: Two pale flames hang over the graves, and between them, if the light is right, a red thread.
運命の赤い糸. The red thread of fate. Cut one and the other calls it back.
Both in one stroke. Or neither.
after: 一蓮托生. To share one lotus in the next life. I think that is all they wanted.

name: Wind
hint: Wind 風: at the end of every turn the wind carries lanterns, umbrellas, ghosts and soul-flames one tile downwind, if the way is clear. Where they burn now is not where they will burn next.
story: In 1274 and again in 1281 the Mongol fleets came for these islands, and twice a great wind scattered them. 神風. People have trusted the wind ever since. You should not.
It moves everything light. Read where things will be, not where they are.
after: 風前の灯火. A lamp before the wind. Today the lamp was theirs.

name: Rain
hint: Rain 雨: lanterns and fire are out and burn nothing. But kappa leave the water and walk the land as they please.
story: Rain on the temple roof. The lanterns hiss and go dark, and the river comes up over its banks, thoughtfully.
The fire is out. That helps.
雨降って地固まる. After rain the ground is firmer. During rain, the kappa can walk on it.
after: 春雨じゃ、濡れて参ろう. It is only spring rain. Let us go and get wet.

name: Deep Snow
hint: Deep snow 雪: every water tile is frozen into ice. You can cross it, sliding. Kappa are held fast where they stand, though they still strike what comes beside them.
story: Snow has been falling all night. The pond is a white floor, and something green is frozen into it up to the shoulders, looking annoyed.
柳に雪折れなし. The willow does not break under snow. Be the willow: let the ice carry you instead of fighting it.
after: The whole pond was a road.
It always was. It only needed the right weather.

name: Night
hint: Night 夜: the rules are as ever, but you see only two tiles around yourself and one around any light. Lanterns and fire show you the board. Put out a lantern and you lose what it lit.
story: 一寸先は闇. One inch ahead, darkness.
I cannot see what is past the lanterns.
Then think before you put one out. 闇夜の提灯: a lantern on a dark night is a friend, even when it is trying to burn you.
after: 明けない夜はない. There is no night that does not end.

name: Shinigami
hint: Shinigami 死神: it drifts toward you through stone, water and everything else, and it has three lives. If it is beside you when a stroke ends, the stage is lost at once, however much ki you have.
story: Something thin is standing at the edge of the lamplight. It has been standing there for some time. It is not in the scroll, and never was.
That one is not a yokai. That one comes for everybody. 生者必滅: all that lives must perish. But not tonight, if you keep your distance and your wits.
Three times. From a long way off.
after: 九死に一生を得る. Nine deaths, and one life kept. It will be back, for both of us. Not today.

name: Shikigami
hint: Shikigami 式神: your brush cannot cut here, but a yokai bound by your circle goes into your hand (up to three). Press 4 and a direction to set the oldest on a tile beside you. It holds that tile, and at the start of every yokai turn it strikes whatever stands within its own reach.
story: Abe no Seimei, the fox's son, kept twelve spirits folded in paper under the Ichijō bridge and called them out when he had need. 式神.
The ones I bind. I can keep them?
You can ask them to stand somewhere. 毒を以て毒を制す: use poison to master poison.
And they will fight for me.
昨日の敵は今日の友. Yesterday's enemy, today's friend. Be polite to them.
after: 急急如律令. Swiftly, as the law commands. That is how Seimei ended every spell.
